about: The cast manifest: one entry per thing that has to be drawn, with the identity tags, the states, the framing and the canvas each one needs. It is a work order, not a config file — nothing reads it at runtime. Feed a row to tools/gen/comfy.mjs and judge the batch (docs/ART-PIPELINE.md §5).

contract.note: Style and quality tags are NOT in this file on purpose. They live in tools/gen/comfy.mjs (STYLE_TAGS, QUALITY_TAGS) and the generator appends them, so a cast row can never drift from the house style. `tags` is identity only; `poseTags` is action only.
contract.styleTags: official art, cel shading, soft shading, vibrant colors, rim lighting, colorful, detailed
contract.qualityTags: masterpiece, high score, great score, absurdres
contract.facing: v3 (2026-09-17). Every subject that appears on a battlefield carries a `facing`. Party, dressphere and ally subjects are "right" (they stand on the left of the field and fight rightward); every boss, enemy and aeon is "left". Portraits are "none" — a HUD head-shot is not on the battlefield and should meet the player's eye. The generator turns this into the camera phrase (FACING_PHRASES in comfy.mjs); pass it as --facing. Direction is the one part of the prompt the checkpoint gets wrong often, so judge every batch for it and mirror a good-but-backwards variant rather than rerolling: docs/handoff/art3-contract.md.

fields.id: Asset id, lowercase kebab. Becomes the folder under public/art/characters/ (or the filename for backdrops and portraits).
fields.kind: party | boss | aeon | dressphere | character | backdrop | portrait
fields.cmd: Which comfy.mjs preset to invoke: character, boss or backdrop.
fields.composition: Default --composition for this subject (states may override).
fields.sizeHint: Default --size. Derived from the sprite cells in research/visual-bible.md §0.4.
fields.tags: Identity tags only, Danbooru order: count, character, series, rating, everything else.
fields.negAdd: Extra negatives for this subject, appended to BASE_NEGATIVE with --negAdd.
fields.refState: Which state is the identity anchor the other states pass to --ref.
fields.states: pose -> { poseTags, optional composition, sizeHint, ref, forceRef, refWeight, refStart, refEnd, notes }.
fields.forceRef: Per-state override: use --ref even though the reference measured mostly one colour (comfy.mjs's monochrome-reference guard would otherwise silently drop it). See docs/concepts/chapters/leblanc/pilot/pilot.md.
fields.notes: What to watch for when judging the batch.
fields.facing: right | left | none. Which way the body is angled, --facing. right = party (stands left, fights right), left = enemy/boss/aeon, none = straight-on (portraits). Defaults if omitted: right for the character preset, left for the boss preset, none for --composition portrait.

poseTagBans.motion lines: Dropped from every pose in this file. On Animagine XL 4.0 it does not draw speed lines — it sprays a coloured swirl around the figure, rembg keeps the swirl as opaque content, and the cutout comes back as the whole 832x1216 frame with baselineY on a ribbon of paint. SPRITE_NEGATIVE bans the splatter as well; both halves of the fix are needed.

workflow: Generate the refState (usually idle) first, --batch 3, and pick a keeper.
Generate every other state with --ref <the keeper> so identity and costume carry over.
Judge facing before anything else on a v3 render: a figure facing the wrong way is unusable no matter how good the costume is, but it is fixable by mirroring, so keep it and flip it.
Judge on costume first, then extra subjects, then cropped limbs, then the cutout (docs/ART-PIPELINE.md §5).
Check baselineY against the feet on any pose with something hanging below them.

subjects.notes: The proof-of-concept could not get Seymour Flux as one image — Animagine knows "seymour guado" and nothing about the Flux form, so three variants all came back as robed Seymour with an aura. v2 splits him: this subject is only the pale torso rising out of the bone frame, mortiorchis is the mount, and the engine composites the two. Generate the torso with --ref public/art/characters/seymour-flux/idle.png so the face and hair match the existing approved render. CANON, and the thing every variant gets wrong: the two long pale shapes rising behind his head are HAIR — two horn-like LOCKS of blue hair swept up and falling down his back — not bone horns, not antlers, not a helmet. Write them as hair every time and put "horns, antlers, helmet" in --negAdd. He is SEATED on Mortiorchis, fused into the bone frame at the waist, never standing and never with legs. His face and bare chest carry pronounced dark VEINS under the skin, which is most of what makes the form read as Flux rather than as robed Seymour.
